mentions.name: Mini Chess Games
mentions.description: A website offering a collection of small chess-based puzzles, such as boards strewn with rocks where the player moves a single piece to a goal square, including a 'radioactive pooping knights' variant. Built with the author's 6-year-old, who acted as product owner.
mentions.source_excerpt: I've been working on https://www.minichessgames.com which I built with my 6 year old (she was the product owner ;). It's a site with a bunch of small puzzles (e.g. imagine a chess board with rocks thrown onto it, then move a single piece to a goal square).

mentions.name: Mini Chess Games
mentions.description: A collection of browser mini-games that teach the movement of chess pieces. The current game is a maze-style challenge where the player reaches a goal square in the minimum number of moves while navigating around rock obstacles, with additional simple games such as battling knights in progress.
mentions.problem: Learning how chess pieces move can be difficult for beginners, such as children.
mentions.audience: Children learning chess piece movements, initially the author's daughter
mentions.source_excerpt:
I've been working on a little game for my daughter to help her learn the movement of chess pieces. https://www.minichessgames.com

It's currently just a "maze" type game where you have to get to a goal square in the minimum number of moves (there are rocks placed on the board to act as obstacles)
